title: Lesson 8: How to Disciple Others
description: Someone once helped you follow Jesus. This lesson shows how to walk alongside another person the way Jesus walked with His disciples, so that what you have received keeps being passed on.

blocks.text: You have learned to pray, listen, serve, share, live for Jesus at work and school, and stand firm in a real spiritual battle. Growing Out is meant to bear fruit in other people, not only in you. This lesson is the next step: making space to sit down with someone as they follow Jesus, then sending them to help someone else.

blocks.alt: An older Paul works with his hands on tent cloth and rope while a young Timothy sits close beside him, listening

blocks.title: Four Generations
blocks.text:
When Paul met Timothy in Lystra, Timothy was already a disciple with a good reputation among the believers (Acts 16:1-2). Paul invited him to travel and serve alongside him. Timothy heard Paul teach and watched how he lived through hardship. Years later Paul reminded him, "You, however, have followed my teaching, my conduct, my aim in life, my faith, my patience, my love, my steadfastness" (2 Timothy 3:10).

Paul did more than give Timothy information. He shared his life and prepared Timothy to lead. Even when they were apart, Paul wrote to instruct and encourage him. Then Paul gave Timothy a charge that reached far beyond the two of them.
and what you have heard from me in the presence of many witnesses entrust to faithful men, who will be able to teach others also.

Notice the four generations: Paul, Timothy, faithful people, and others. Paul was helping Timothy depend on Jesus and preparing him for his own personal ministry. He sat with Timothy, then sent him to sit with others. In the same way, someone has helped you follow Jesus. This lesson is about how God might use you to disciple another person to become a disciple-maker.
8.1 - Who has helped you grow in love for God and others? What did that person do?
Jesus Calls Ordinary People to Make Disciples

Jesus chose twelve disciples "so that they might be with him and he might send them out to preach" (Mark 3:14). Before He ever sent them out, they studied Jesus' perfect balance of truth and love. They heard His teaching (word), watched His compassion for people (deed), and they practiced the way of Jesus. As they matured, He gave them appropriate challenges to serve, and when they came back, they were encouraged as they told Him all they had done and taught (Mark 6:30). Jesus was forming ordinary people who would carry His message and be sent to others.

After His resurrection, Jesus commanded His followers to make disciples, baptizing them and "teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you" (Matthew 28:19-20). The goal was never just that someone would know more Bible facts. Discipleship helps a person grow in love for God and love for others, and learn to obey Jesus in everyday life.

You may feel unqualified because you still have questions and still struggle with sin, but so did the people Jesus first called. You do not need to be a perfect Christian or have every answer. You just need to keep following Jesus, care about another person, and share what you are learning. And you will not do it alone. Jesus ends the Great Commission with a promise: "I am with you always" (Matthew 28:20).
Sit Down Together

Discipleship grows when people sit down together, whether it is one friend over coffee or a few others around a table in your small group. Sitting together gives people room to ask honest questions, face their struggles, practice obeying Jesus, and celebrate progress. Watch what happens at one table.
Make SPACES

Did you see the word take shape? Make SPACES: Study, Practice, Appropriate Challenge, Encourage, Send. Each step has one word to hold onto. We study to learn, practice to talk, give an appropriate challenge to do, encourage to keep on, and send so others will go. Jesus did every one of these with His disciples, and by His grace you can do them with someone else.
Study: Learn

Open God's Word together and learn. Growing Together gives you a path to follow, so start with the lessons that fit the person, whether that means the foundations in 101 or a topic from the 200 series. Read the lesson, look at Scripture, ask what it means, and pray. Jesus did this with two discouraged friends on the road to Emmaus, opening the Scriptures until their hearts burned within them (Luke 24:27, 32). The goal is not to finish pages. It is to help someone know Jesus and love Him more.
Practice: Talk

Faith grows stronger when we put it into words. Practice talking about spiritual things in a safe and loving place: praying out loud, explaining a passage, or telling the story of how you came to follow Jesus. You might say, "Let's practice sharing your testimony. You can share yours with me first." Later, let them lead a question or a section of the lesson while you help them prepare. They learn by watching, trying, and trying again.
Appropriate Challenge: Do

Knowing is not the same as doing. Jesus said the wise builder is the one who hears His words and does them (Matthew 7:24). Look at the person with hopeful eyes and say something like, "I see in you a heart for people. I want to challenge you to start a conversation about Jesus with someone this week." A newer believer may be ready to pray aloud or share a testimony. Someone further along may be ready to lead part of a Growing Together lesson. A good challenge stretches someone without leaving them on their own.
Encourage: Keep On

Discipleship is not a one-time event, so encouragement is what helps people keep on. Ask what happened, listen, pray, and celebrate the courage it took to try. If it did not go well, stay close and help them choose another step. Paul kept strengthening Timothy through his letters long after they were apart. Encouragement is not an extra after the real work. It is part of how people grow.
Send: Go

Then send them. Jesus told His disciples, "As the Father has sent me, even so I am sending you" (John 20:21). You might say, "You are ready to sit down with someone else. Would you invite one person to begin Growing Together with you?" You are not handing them a title or asking them to become an expert. You are helping them care for another person the way someone cared for them, using the same lessons and the same SPACES. And you do not disappear. You keep cheering them on as they go.
8.2 - Think about the person who helped you grow. Which of these five did they do with you: learn, talk, do, keep on, or go? Which one do you most want to pass on to someone else?
Addition or Multiplication

When one person helps another grow in Jesus, that is a beautiful thing, and it is worth celebrating every time. But Paul asked Timothy for something more. He wanted faithful people "who will be able to teach others also." That is the difference between addition and multiplication.

Picture it this way. If you helped one new person grow in Jesus every year by yourself, in ten years you would have walked with ten people. That is a life well spent. But if you disciple one person this year, and next year each of you disciples one more, and everyone keeps doing the same, in ten years there would be more than a thousand disciple-makers. Addition gathers people around you. Multiplication sends people out from you, and it keeps growing long after you.

This is what Jesus had in mind all along. He told us to make disciples, "teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you" (Matthew 28:20), and one of the things He commanded is to make disciples. A disciple who learns to obey everything Jesus commanded will make disciples too. We disciple others so they can disciple others.
Life on Life

Multiplication does not happen through information alone. Paul and Timothy wrote this to a young church together: "we were ready to share with you not only the gospel of God but also our own selves, because you had become very dear to us" (1 Thessalonians 2:8). That is life-on-life ministry. It takes words and life, truth and love, shared around the same table.

Here is a picture that may help. Going through a study like this for the first time is like tasting great food. Leading someone else through it is like chewing it up and consuming it, so that it becomes part of you. As you think through how to help another person understand it, and then help them be sent to teach it to others, God changes you even more.
Your Appropriate Challenge

So where do you start? Use this Growing Together Discipleship Series and invite one person, or a few, to spend time together helping each other grow. Look for someone who is faithful, available, and teachable. They do not need to know much or look impressive. Meet once a week or every other week, open a lesson, and walk SPACES together.

If you are going through this lesson with someone right now, look across the table. One of you has been leading, and the other has been receiving. This may be your appropriate challenge: it is time to be sent. You have tasted the food, and now you get to serve it to someone else. The person who has been discipling you can say, "I will be here to help and encourage you all along the way," and mean it. In the sessions ahead, we will keep talking about who you can disciple.
8.3 - Who is one faithful, available, and teachable person you could invite to go through Growing Together with you? Write down their name and when you could ask them.
God Gives the Growth

Think of an orchard. A gardener can prepare the soil, plant, water, and care for a young tree, but the gardener cannot make it live. Paul wrote, "I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth" (1 Corinthians 3:6). Your job is not to change another person's heart. Only God can do that. Your part is to make space, open His Word, walk with them, send them, and depend on the Holy Spirit. Some conversations will feel fruitful and others will feel slow, so keep praying and keep caring.
8.4 - Dream for a moment. If the person you named one day disciples someone else, and that person does the same, what might God do through your one yes in the next five years?
Lesson 8 Review

Paul poured his life into Timothy, and Timothy passed it on to faithful people who would teach others also. Jesus calls ordinary people to make disciples who make disciples, and He promises to be with us always. You can make SPACES: study to learn, practice to talk, give an appropriate challenge to do, encourage to keep on, and send so others will go. When we make space for one person and send them to do the same, addition becomes multiplication, and the worship of God grows one table at a time.
In the next lesson, you will consider the people God places beside you in His mission, from your church to the ends of the earth.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What is a prayer request for this week?
Further reading: The Disciple Maker's Handbook by Bobby Harrington and Josh Robert Patrick; Discipleship Essentials by Greg Ogden; and The Master Plan of Evangelism by Robert Coleman.
